nodes.title: Barnette graph G
nodes.statement: Cubic, bipartite, 3-connected, planar. The claim is that G has a Hamiltonian cycle, and more: one that avoids any prescribed edge.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Dual Eulerian triangulation (T, t0, e0)
nodes.statement: T = G* is a simple sphere triangulation with faces coloured black and white. Root it at a black face t0 with an edge e0. Vertices of G are faces of T, faces of G are vertices of T.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Two induced trees
nodes.statement: The goal in dual form. G has a Hamiltonian cycle avoiding e0* if and only if V(T) splits into two sets, each inducing a tree, with both ends of e0 in one of them (Stein 1971; APSW 2016).

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: States
nodes.statement: A state is a bijection s from the bounded black faces A to the non-root vertices X with s(t) a corner of t. It is a perfect matching of the incidence graph B. |A| = |X| = n.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: A pair (r, s)
nodes.statement: Two states that differ at every face. The partner r is the certificate that orients Q_s: the edge opposite s(t) in t is directed out of r(t).

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Disk identity
nodes.statement: A directed cycle of state edges of length h with l black faces of its disk along it has 2l - h = -3. Equivalently its disk holds exactly one more white face than black faces.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Signed measure on pairs
nodes.statement: Every pair gets a sign (i^J in O, (-1)^cw in L, epsilon in T). Reversing a cycle of D(r, s) flips it, and reversing a cycle of Q_s flips it. The whole proof is one signed sum over pairs, weighted by a function of s.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Cancellation of cyclic Q_s
nodes.statement: Sum with s fixed. If Q_s has a cycle, reversing it changes r, keeps s and the weight, and flips the sign. So only pairs with Q_s a forest survive.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Nonvanishing
nodes.statement: Sum with the undirected cycle set D fixed. With weights whose circulation is positive on every counterclockwise spoke cycle, the lowest-order term is a positive count of the covers with fewest cycles.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Forest pair / tree matching
nodes.statement: A pair with Q_s a forest. Equivalently a state s with H - s a spanning tree of the spoke graph. Equivalently a state with exactly one partner.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Incidence tree H - s
nodes.statement: Delete the n matched spokes from the spoke graph H. What is left is a spanning tree: every black centre keeps two spokes, t0 keeps three.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: White-face tree
nodes.statement: The duals of the n deleted spokes form a spanning tree on the white faces (tree-cotree duality in the plane).

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Selected edges P
nodes.statement: Root the white tree at y0, the white face across e0. Each tree edge selects one side of its black face. With e0 this is one edge in every face of T, a perfect matching of G.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Jordan curve
nodes.statement: E(G) - P is 2-regular. It is a single cycle, hence a Jordan curve on the sphere, and its two sides are the two induced trees.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Gluing
nodes.statement: If a separating triangle blocks the state method at this root, cut along it, cap both sides, solve each with the cap edge prescribed, and glue.

nodes.status: established (LIT: waypoint of the 2026 proofs; the papers are unrefereed preprints)
nodes.title: Hamiltonian cycle
nodes.statement: Every Barnette graph has a Hamiltonian cycle avoiding any prescribed edge (O Theorem 1.1, Corollary 7.1).

nodes.title: Step S0: Dualise and root
nodes.statement: 3-connected cubic plane graphs are the duals of simple triangulations, and bipartite means the faces of T 2-colour. This is the only place 3-connectivity is used.
nodes.note: No freedom in the statement. Li keeps the primal language through the auxiliary graph aux(G); the objects are the same.

nodes.title: Step TG: Restate the goal
nodes.statement: A Hamiltonian cycle of G is a Jordan curve; the faces of G on each side are vertices of T inducing a tree. Known since Stein. All pre-2026 attacks tried to cross here directly.
nodes.note: This is the edge that 57 years of partial results worked on. None of them reaches all Barnette graphs.

nodes.title: Step ST: Define states and count
nodes.statement: Euler's formula gives equally many black and white faces k and k + 2 vertices, so |A| = |X| = k - 1. Without this equality there is nothing to match.
nodes.note: States are Tutte's trinity states with the colours swapped. Their number is a determinant.

nodes.title: Step A: Find two disjoint states
nodes.statement: The incidence graph B must contain two edge-disjoint perfect matchings. This is where a separating triangle can obstruct, and the only place the papers use 'no separating triangle'.
nodes.note: Four published arguments (flow with a density bound; Ore deficiency with a minimal set; the exact criterion; Hall on a gadget in the Lean proof). They prove different amounts.

nodes.title: Step B: Prove the disk identity
nodes.statement: Euler's formula on the disk, a signed count of sides, and B = I + l, which holds because a state is a bijection.
nodes.note: One double count in all three papers, on triangles (O, T) or on hexagons of the spoke graph (L). A second derivation, as the theorem of turning tangents for an angle structure, is proved in the topology folder and unreviewed.

nodes.title: Step C: Sign the pairs
nodes.statement: Define the sign and show that both reversals flip it. The disk identity is used twice here: on the cycles of D and on the cycle of Q_s.
nodes.note: Three notations for one sign. The complex phase is packaging; a real sign is enough.

nodes.title: Step K: Cancel with s fixed
nodes.statement: The reversed cycle of Q_s must be chosen from s alone, so that the map is an involution that keeps the weight.
nodes.note: All three papers use the same involution. It is the statement that a twisted incidence determinant of Q_s vanishes on a cycle.

nodes.title: Step N: Show the total is not zero
nodes.statement: Weights that depend on s only and separate the two orientations of every D-cycle. Then group by D and find a term that cannot cancel.
nodes.note: The widest step: five published arguments, two more proved here, and a long list of refuted shortcuts. Every route that works still minimises over the number of cycles.

nodes.title: Step D: Compare the two evaluations
nodes.statement: The same sum is supported on forest pairs (by K) and is not zero (by N). So a forest pair exists.
nodes.note: The comparison is one line. No canonical forest pair is known: every extremal choice tried is refuted.

nodes.title: Step U: Unsigned routes (bypass)
nodes.statement: Find a tree matching with no signed sum: as a prescribed-degree spanning tree, a three-matroid intersection, a constrained white tree, a point of the state lattice.
nodes.note: Many exact reformulations are proved. None has an existence argument. Every relaxation tried drops a constraint and is refuted by a small example.

nodes.title: Step R: One root per component
nodes.statement: The partner gives out-degree one at non-roots and zero at roots, so a tree component of Q_s has exactly one root. With the three spokes of t0 this makes H - s a spanning tree.
nodes.note: Same count in all three papers. A forest without a partner is not enough.

nodes.title: Step E: Tree-cotree duality
nodes.statement: The complement of a spanning tree of a plane graph is a spanning tree of the dual.
nodes.note: Rigid as a statement. The Lean proof skips the node: it selects P inside G and never builds the white tree.

nodes.title: Step E2: Root at y0 and select
nodes.statement: Orient the white tree towards y0; the edge above each white face selects one side of a black face.
nodes.note: Rigid. The three papers select the same set P.

nodes.title: Step F: Show P leaves one cycle
nodes.statement: P has one edge in every face of T, so E(G) - P is 2-regular. It must be connected.
nodes.note: Two published arguments. O, T and the Lean proof count against the disk identity (a third use). Li uses an innermost cycle and needs neither the disk identity nor the partner.

nodes.title: Step J2: Sides of the curve
nodes.statement: The two sides of the Jordan curve are the two induced trees, and e0 lies in one of them.
nodes.note: Li skips this node and glues Hamiltonian cycles directly.

nodes.title: Step G: Cut at separating triangles
nodes.statement: The prescribed edge is what lets two solutions agree on the cap. An unbounded prescription would be NP-hard.
nodes.note: Same induction in all three papers, known since Kelmans 1986. The trees paper cuts less often.

nodes.title: Step G2: Conclude
nodes.statement: Induction on the number of vertices, or a minimum counterexample.
nodes.note: None.

nodes.title: duality; 3-connectivity gives a simple T
nodes.statement: The dual of a 3-connected cubic plane graph is a simple triangulation; G bipartite iff T Eulerian iff the faces of T 2-colour iff the vertices 3-colour.
where: O proof of Thm 1.1; APSW 2016 Section 1
nodes.status: established (LIT: 2026 preprint or its formalisation, unrefereed)

nodes.title: stay in G with aux(G)
nodes.statement: Li works in the primal graph with the face/black-vertex incidence graph. aux(G) is T with a centre in every face.
nodes.status: established (LIT: 2026 preprint or its formalisation, unrefereed)

nodes.title: 3-connectivity enters only here
nodes.statement: In O, 3-connectivity is used once, to exclude loops and parallel edges in the dual. Simplicity is then used in the flow bound and the gluing.

nodes.title: drop bipartite
nodes.statement: Without bipartiteness there is no proper face colouring of T, so states are not defined.
nodes.lesson: Odd degrees obstruct the algebra itself, before any question of Hamiltonicity. Best max-cut colourings of K4, BBL38 and Tutte's graph leave 2, 7 and 9 monochromatic adjacencies.
nodes.note: Smallest known counterexample: K4 (4 vertices): the dual has all degrees odd. Tutte's 46-vertex graph is the non-Hamiltonian witness.

nodes.title: drop 3-connectivity
nodes.statement: A 2-connected cubic bipartite planar graph can be non-Hamiltonian. Its dual has parallel edges.
nodes.lesson: The proof stops at the pair: the 26-vertex theta of three cubes-minus-an-edge has 8 states and no disjoint pair at each of its 26 roots. The disk identity itself survives in the multimap.
nodes.note: Smallest known counterexample: theta of three copies of cube-minus-edge, 26 vertices (minimum by Asano-Saito-Exoo-Harary 1982, abstract only).

nodes.title: other surfaces
nodes.statement: On an orientable surface of genus g, |A| - |X| = 2g, so states with three roots do not exist for g > 0, and the two-tree target is impossible on the torus by an edge count.
nodes.lesson: The first obstruction is cardinality. A surface version needs a different state and a different target (one edge per triangle with connected complementary dual).
nodes.note: Smallest known counterexample: 3 x 3 periodic triangular grid on the torus: no two induced trees, yet the dual has 36 Hamiltonian cycles.

nodes.title: Stein 1971; APSW Lemma 5
nodes.statement: T* is Hamiltonian iff V(T) splits into two induced forests, which for triangulations are two induced trees.
where: Stein, Pacific J. Math. 37 (1971), Thm 2.2; APSW 2016, Lemma 5

nodes.title: prescribed edge: O Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: With e0 inside one tree the cycle avoids e0*. This is the H- form of Kelmans and Hertel, equivalent to the conjecture.
nodes.status: established (LIT: 2026 preprint or its formalisation, unrefereed)

nodes.title: face-size results (Goodey; Schnieders)
nodes.statement: Hamiltonicity when all faces have size at most 6 (Goodey), at most 8 (Schnieders, 339 million computer cases). Partial: local reductions cannot see 3-connectivity, which becomes necessary at face size 10.

nodes.title: computer search to 90 vertices
nodes.statement: All Barnette graphs up to 90 vertices are Hamiltonian.

nodes.title: trees of faces (Feder-Subi)
nodes.statement: Contract a colour class of faces and look for a quasi spanning tree of faces. Polynomial when the remaining faces have 2 or 3 sides, NP-complete in general. The closest older relative of the incidence tree.

nodes.title: A-trails, braces, book embeddings
nodes.statement: Equivalent formulations in other languages. None supplied an existence mechanism.

nodes.title: trees from colour classes
nodes.statement: Build a permeating subtree containing all or none of a colour class of the vertex 3-colouring.
nodes.lesson: APSW give Eulerian triangulations in which every permeating subtree contains at least k and misses at least k vertices of every colour class. The trees of the 2026 proofs come from a matching, not from colour classes.
nodes.note: Smallest known counterexample: APSW 2016, family for every k (not reconstructed here).

nodes.title: Grinberg obstruction
nodes.statement: Use Grinberg's formula with a modulus to decide Hamiltonicity.
where: research/2026-11-14_opus_history-literature/WHAT-WAS-HARD.md 2; research/2026-11-14_opus_route-graph-theory/PROOFS.md (Grinberg's identity is automatic for two induced trees)
nodes.lesson: A Barnette graph has f_4 = 6 + sum (k/2 - 3) f_k, so at least six faces of weight 2 and the classical modulus argument cannot apply. PROVED-HERE in the history folder.
nodes.note: Smallest known counterexample: Any Barnette graph: at least six 4-faces.

nodes.title: induced-forest completion
nodes.statement: Start from a large induced forest and exchange vertices until both sides are trees.
nodes.vivid: Farthest from the pair machinery. The general Albertson-Berman conjecture cannot be an input: 2026 preprints report counterexamples.
nodes.test: Enumerate maximum induced forests on small Eulerian triangulations and look for a trapped configuration.

nodes.title: nodal domains of eigenvectors
nodes.statement: Sign patterns of Laplacian eigenvectors of T almost never give two induced trees (predicted below 5 per cent).
nodes.test: Run over the sample of the topology agent; outcome pending in topo/ROUTES.md.

nodes.title: Euler count |A| = |X|
nodes.statement: k black faces, k white faces, k + 2 vertices, so n = k - 1 on both sides of B.
nodes.status: established (LIT: 2026 preprint or its formalisation, unrefereed)

nodes.title: states = trinity states; number = |det K_B|
nodes.statement: All states have one permutation sign, so their number is |det K_B|, Tutte's magic number, the number of arborescences of each of the three trinity graphs.

nodes.title: states form a distributive lattice
nodes.statement: Clock moves connect all states. The tree matchings are a subset of this lattice with no known description.

nodes.title: uniform sampling of states
nodes.statement: Because all extensions of a partial matching have one sign, residual determinants count them, and a state can be sampled uniformly in polynomial time. This does not sample tree matchings.
nodes.status: established: proved here (1 independent AI referee; human check pending)

nodes.title: every avoiding cycle comes from a tree matching
nodes.statement: If every Hamiltonian cycle avoiding e0* came from a tree matching, known Hamiltonicity results would give pairs with no flow argument.
where: posed in research/2026-11-14_fable_dependency-graph/skeleton.md A2; refuted by research/2026-11-14_fable_route-combinatorics/ROUTES.md 12 (E8) and research/2026-11-14_astra_limits/examples/prism_recovery.json
nodes.lesson: The recovery map is injective and not onto. A cycle avoiding e0* always defines a state, and that state is a tree matching or has no partner at all. Most avoiding cycles are of the second kind (ratio up to 26).

nodes.statement: With the vertex 3-colouring c, delta(v, w) = c(w) - c(v) mod 3. The identity says the disk of a directed state cycle holds one more white face than black faces; the colouring map has degree -1 on it.

nodes.title: checked on every enumerated cycle
nodes.statement: All disk equalities hold on every cycle enumerated, with all outgoing choices for n <= 6.

nodes.title: drop bijectivity
nodes.statement: Let each black face choose a corner with no injectivity requirement.
nodes.lesson: With defect d = B - I - l the identity becomes 2l - h = -3 - 3d. The state condition is exactly d = 0. Every interior vertex must be covered once.
nodes.note: Smallest known counterexample: 9 vertices: a directed 4-cycle with delta-sum 0; vertex 8 is used twice, d = -1.

nodes.title: integer lift of Kasteleyn's sign lemma
nodes.statement: The faces of the spoke graph are hexagons, 6 = 2 mod 4, which is Kasteleyn's condition. The common sign of all states uses only the parity part of the disk identity.
nodes.vivid: The disk identity may be a flatness condition for a Z/4 or complex signing of spokes.
nodes.test: Derive t_out - t_in = 3 from a flatness condition for such a signing.

nodes.title: discrete Morse theory
nodes.statement: Read the state as a pairing of black faces with vertices in the disk and compute the degree from the unpaired cells.
nodes.vivid: B = I + l looks like a cancellation of cells.
nodes.test: Write the pairing as a discrete vector field and check that one white face is always left over.

nodes.title: peel the disk
nodes.statement: Remove a boundary vertex with its matched black face and show 2l - h does not change.
nodes.vivid: An inductive proof with a picture per step.
nodes.test: Implement the peeling on enumerated cycles.

nodes.title: Grinberg count made rigid by a matching
nodes.statement: 3(B - W) = 2l - h is a Grinberg balance in the dual; the bijection adds B = I + l.
nodes.vivid: Places the one new lemma next to the oldest tool of the subject.

nodes.title: zero, vertex-only or face-only weights
nodes.statement: Use weights alpha_t + beta_v, or none.
nodes.lesson: Such weights are pure gauge: every state has the same total, and the signed count is 0 = 0. What is needed is positive circulation on cycles, not positive weights.

nodes.title: parity or mod p count without weights
nodes.statement: Show the number of tree matchings is odd, or nonzero mod p.
nodes.lesson: The number of tree matchings is always even (the two signs balance), and T = P - 2 N_1 mod 4 is compatible with T = 0. The weighted sum is the refinement that works; the first degree at which anything survives is cmin. No modulus among 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 gives a universally nonzero residue; the positive counts seen are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 22.

nodes.title: tree pair among the fewest-cycle pairs
nodes.statement: Among the pairs with the fewest D-cycles one has Q_s a forest; or every cycle cover D has a forest orientation.

The leading coefficient is nonzero because of the fewest-cycle covers, but the surviving pairs can live in other covers. A statement that held on 1794 cases failed at the next size. (Scope as corrected by the referee.)

nodes.title: highest or lowest partnered state

nodes.title: one cycle always suffices

nodes.title: cubes of tree matchings; sign = parity of rank
nodes.statement: Tree matchings split into cubes of dimension cmin; or eps(s) = (-1)^omega(s) up to a constant.

nodes.title: ordinary determinant, all face variables 1

nodes.title: allow doubled edges (standard double dimers)

nodes.title: positive semidefinite blocks
